ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Under natural conditions, the trends of the photosynthetic rate and respiration rate of the leaves of a certain plant changing with temperature are shown in the figure. Answer the following questions. Answer the question: At temperature d, will the dry weight of this plant body remain unchanged?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis represents temperature, and the vertical axis represents the CO₂ absorption/release rate; the photosynthetic rate curve first rises as temperature increases, reaches a relatively high value near b, and then declines; the respiration rate curve gradually rises as temperature increases. In the figure, near d, the two curves intersect, indicating that the photosynthetic rate and respiration rate of this leaf are roughly equal. Then reason: What the question asks is whether the dry weight of “this plant body” remains unchanged, rather than only asking about the net photosynthetic rate of this leaf at temperature d. The change in the dry weight of the plant body depends on the accumulation and consumption of organic matter in the whole plant, including the respiratory consumption of organs other than leaves, such as roots and stems; under natural conditions, at night photosynthesis cannot be carried out but respiration still proceeds. Therefore, even if at point d the leaf photosynthetic rate and the leaf respiration rate are equal, it cannot show that the dry weight of the whole plant body remains unchanged.
